title: PUT PATCH and DELETE
summary: Methods have different intended meanings. PUT commonly replaces a resource representation; PATCH changes part; DELETE requests removal.
introduction: Methods have different intended meanings. PUT commonly replaces a resource representation; PATCH changes part; DELETE requests removal. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Methods have different intended meanings. PUT commonly replaces a resource representation; PATCH changes part; DELETE requests removal.

blocks.code:
PUT /notes/3 -> replace the note representation
PATCH /notes/3 -> apply a partial change
DELETE /notes/3 -> request removal
blocks.title: PUT PATCH and DELETE

blocks.text: The API documentation must explain the exact body and behaviour. A delete example is a plan, not permission to delete real data.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Choose a method for changing only a note's color under a documented partial-update API.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A method name alone does not tell you all the service's business rules.
For more detail later, use this [Postman further reading](https://learning.postman.com/docs/getting-started/overview/).
